claims.statement: A 2024 multisite EEG methods paper recommends an immediate first-pass quality check because event-code and hardware problems can otherwise affect many participants before final analysis occurs months or years later.

FDA guidance for digital technologies in clinical investigations emphasizes fit-for-purpose verification, validation, data integrity, and consistent data quality, supporting a paid quality-control layer for sensor-derived trial data.
Hypothesis: small studies will buy per-study QA when the service is cheaper than replacing even a few unusable participants and can work across their existing EEG hardware.

contrary_evidence: EEGLAB, MNE, PREP, and lab-specific scripts make much of the technical checking available as open-source building blocks.
Large sponsored trials already use central EEG labs, while academic studies may have little procurement budget.

economics.acquisition_route: Publish a benchmark on public EEG datasets, then obtain channel referrals from one hardware vendor and two core facilities
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 25 studies per year at a 150k PLN blended contract yield 3.75M PLN revenue and roughly 1.5M PLN EBITDA by year 6. A defensible scientific-QA provider at 5x EBITDA and 70% founder ownership implies about 5.25M PLN equity in years 7 to 9.
economics.founder_time: 15 to 20 hours weekly through validation, then 10 to 15 hours with a contracted EEG reviewer
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 60% to 75% after expert review; automated ingest and exception-only review drive margin
economics.payback: Avoiding recollection or loss of a handful of participants can cover the service, but the value must be quantified per protocol
economics.pricing: 25,000 to 50,000 PLN setup plus 300 to 900 PLN per recording, or 90,000 to 250,000 PLN fixed per study
economics.retention_or_repeat: Studies recur by phase and protocol; CROs and sponsors can standardize the gate across programs and sites

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned artifact and protocol-deviation library indexed by hardware, task, site, population, and corrective action
fingerprint.customer: Boutique CROs, neurotech startups, and investigator-led European studies collecting EEG across multiple sites
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: EEG hardware vendors, core facilities, boutique CRO partnerships, and reproducible methods benchmarks
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Validated automated checks, cross-site dashboard, and bounded expert QA sold per study
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The sponsor, CRO, or principal investigator pays at study setup and per accepted recording batch
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A participant recording finishes and the study team needs to know within 48 hours whether acquisition or protocol issues require correction

founder_fit: Unusually strong founder-market fit from neuroscience, EEG, data science, and AI experience. Work is analytical, remote, and compatible with part-time delivery; a medical-student partner can help interpret clinical workflow boundaries but must not substitute for trial QA expertise.
risks: False negatives can allow irrecoverable data loss; every report needs explicit scope and human escalation.
Raw EEG and trial metadata can be sensitive health and research data.
The founder could drift into labor-intensive custom analysis rather than a repeatable gate.

structure.commercial_archetype: Scientific quality-control service with software leverage
structure.control_point: The accept-or-correct decision issued within 48 hours of each EEG acquisition
structure.critical_dependency: Sponsors must accept validated automated metrics plus bounded expert review across heterogeneous EEG systems

thesis: Provide a hardware-agnostic, human-reviewed EEG quality gate that runs immediately after each recording rather than months later during analysis. It would detect lost or garbled event codes, bad channels, artifact burden, trial-count shortfalls, protocol drift, and site-specific deviations, then return a red-amber-green report before the next participant. The beachhead is boutique CROs, neurotech startups, and investigator-led multicenter studies too small for a central EEG lab; it is research QA, not diagnosis or endpoint interpretation.
title: First-48-Hour EEG Quality Gate for Small Multisite Trials
uncertainties: Number of fundable small multicenter EEG studies in Europe and their QA budgets.
Whether hardware heterogeneity can be supported without expensive protocol-by-protocol work.
What level of validation sponsors require before relying on automated flags.
